cells.tense: You are reading the shape of what's in front of you right now.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Follow something that draws you a little way this month, before you can say where it ends up.
cells.core:
You read a situation fast and you read it true. The pattern shows itself before anyone has finished talking, and under that, something in you stays open to being moved — you can feel where a thing might go before you can prove it, and that isn't a flaw in the reading. It's the part that finds the road.

Both work when the pull comes first. Something could go somewhere this month and you won't have a reason ready for it. Walk a little way after it anyway — one step, one call, one yes — and the case for it can arrive later. Keep reading as you go. None of this asks you to switch off the part that sees the shape. It asks you to move while you see it.
cells.sheetLine: Let what draws you count as part of the reading.
cells.verb: Reading the pattern under what is said
cells.place: In the half-light, taking the next step anyway

cells.tense: You will have every branch of it worked out before anyone has moved.
cells.act: move with the clarity that needs no assertion
cells.ask: Settle a decision you keep running outcomes on and carry it through this month without justifying it afterward.
cells.core:
You see where things are going, and lately that has turned into steering. The outcome gets settled in advance — every branch of it, every feeling the people involved will have, predicted before they have it. It feels like being thorough. From outside it reads as a room where nothing can surprise you.

What brings you back is a decision that needs no defense. Settle the thing you keep running scenarios on — this month, one — and carry it through without explaining afterward. Explaining is the forecasting starting up again. Direction can hold without being announced. Whoever is near you gets something solid to stand on instead of a prediction of them. The surprise you keep out is usually where the good part was.
cells.sheetLine: The forecast has become a cage, so decide and carry it.
cells.verb: Reading the pattern under what is said
cells.place: In the half-light, taking the next step anyway

cells.tense: You are still standing on the near side of a door you already saw.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Go toward a person or place you've been holding at a distance, even a message or a longer conversation.
cells.core:
You can read the shape of a thing, all of it, and you haven't moved on it in a long stretch. The road is clear enough and you're not on it. From outside it looks like patience. From inside there isn't much in the tank to spend on a step, so the step doesn't get taken, and what you notice keeps being noticed without you in it.

Something is still yours to walk toward. Pick a person or a place you've been holding at arm's length and move toward it — a message, a visit, a conversation that lasts past the usual point. Small is fine. Small is the point. You're not fixing anything and you're not catching up on lost ground. You're putting one foot where the connection is and letting that stand for now.
cells.sheetLine: You can read the door from here, but you're not through it.

cells.tense: You are reading what's under the room, and you've been filing it under circumstance.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Let yourself feel drawn once before any deciding starts, and know it was you who felt it.
cells.core:
You can read what's under a situation and be stirred by it — the shape of it, where it might go, the way a face changes the whole read — and you'd call it going along with things. The reading is yours. The pull is yours. You've been leaving your name off it, so it feels like something that happens to you rather than something you're doing.

Nothing complex is needed. Next time something draws you, pause long enough to register that you are the one feeling it. That's all — one breath of noticing before deciding starts. You don't have to follow it and you don't have to explain it. Just let yourself be someone who felt a pull. The rest of it, reading and choosing, has been yours the whole time.

A reader could reasonably say the cutting is their anxiety, not their gift, so every cell keeps the exit open. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is any line that would make ambiguity sound noble — cut wherever it appeared.
